titleTemplate: Improve editorial curation and organization
claim: Clear editorial organization helps readers find the useful parts of a page and makes the page's unique contribution easier to assess.
sourceCitation: Cyrus Shepard, Zyppy Signal, Content Effort: visible editorial curation is a signal of unique value.

titleTemplate: Add visible first-party evidence
claim: First-party information, documented examples, and original evidence can make a page more useful than a summary of commonly available facts.
sourceCitation: Cyrus Shepard, Zyppy Signal, Content Effort: original information and evidence of work signal unique value.

titleTemplate: Document the work behind important claims
claim: Visible methodology and supporting artifacts help readers evaluate how a conclusion, example, or data point was produced.
sourceCitation: Cyrus Shepard, Zyppy Signal, Content Effort: methodology, testing, screenshots, and interviews show evidence of work.

titleTemplate: Put helpful information before filler
claim: Leading with direct helpful information makes the page more useful to readers than generic scene-setting or filler.
sourceCitation: Cyrus Shepard, Zyppy Signal, Content Effort: direct helpful information should appear before filler.

titleTemplate: Add analysis, trade-offs, and informed perspective
claim: Analysis of trade-offs and practical constraints can provide more value than a shallow retelling of common information.
sourceCitation: Cyrus Shepard, Zyppy Signal, Content Effort: high-quality discussion and informed perspective go beyond common facts.

titleTemplate: Add concrete statistics
claim: Statistics addition is identified by KDD 2024 as one of the top-performing content optimizations for visibility in generative-engine responses.
sourceCitation: Aggarwal, Murahari, Rajpurohit et al., "GEO: Generative Engine Optimization", KDD 2024 — Statistics Addition is highlighted as a top-performing content-optimization method (§4, Table 1).
notes: The paper does not publish a per-method aggregate lift number we will attribute to this individual recommendation. Headline result reported in the paper is 'up to 41% improvement on Position-Adjusted Word Count' for the best-performing method overall. Per-method numbers previously displayed (e.g. '+33.9%') were not traceable to the paper and have been removed pending an internal benchmark.

titleTemplate: Cite {prevYear}/{currentYear} statistics
claim: Generative engines preferentially cite content with recent dated statistics, treating recency markers as a freshness signal independent of the page's own publish date.
sourceCitation: Practitioner consensus 2025-2026 (Profound, Frase, Search Engine Land); no controlled study located that publishes the specific freshness-citation correlation.
notes: Previously displayed as '83% of commercial AI citations come from sources updated in past 12 months' — that figure is widely repeated in industry blog posts but not traceable to a primary source we can cite. Queue for internal benchmark: re-audit a sample of URLs after their statistics are updated to current-year values and measure citation-count delta.

titleTemplate: Add expert quotes with named attribution
claim: Quotation addition (named-attribution direct quotes from credible sources) is identified by KDD 2024 as one of the top-performing content optimizations for AI-engine visibility.
sourceCitation: Aggarwal, Murahari, Rajpurohit et al., "GEO: Generative Engine Optimization", KDD 2024 — Quotation Addition is highlighted as a top-performing content-optimization method (§4, Table 1).
notes: The paper does not publish a per-method aggregate lift number we will attribute to this individual recommendation. Headline result reported in the paper is 'up to 41% improvement on Position-Adjusted Word Count' for the best-performing method overall (best-method best-metric, not per-method). Per-method numbers previously displayed (e.g. '+32%') were not traceable to the paper and have been removed pending an internal benchmark.

titleTemplate: Add 2-5 outbound links to authoritative sources
claim: Adding outbound citations to credible sources (Cite Sources) is identified by KDD 2024 as one of the top-performing content optimizations for AI-engine visibility, with effect size dependent on the page's current SERP position.
sourceCitation: Aggarwal, Murahari, Rajpurohit et al., "GEO: Generative Engine Optimization", KDD 2024 — Cite Sources is highlighted as a top-performing content-optimization method (§4, Table 1); §4.2 / Table 3 reports the effect is strongly conditioned on SERP position.
notes: Headline result reported in the paper is 'up to 41% improvement on Position-Adjusted Word Count' for the best-performing method overall (best-method best-metric, not per-method). Instead of a single per-method lift, the paper reports SERP-position-conditioned effects for Cite Sources specifically (e.g. +115.1% visibility for rank-5 sites, -30.3% for rank-1 sites). Per-method number previously displayed (e.g. '+30.3%') misread the paper's negative finding for top-ranked sites as a positive lift and has been removed. SERP-conditioned lift is captured as a methodology note for a future product feature; not surfaced as a recommendation lift figure.

titleTemplate: Lead with a 40-60 word direct answer
claim: Generative engines extract opening statements far more often than buried conclusions, making the first paragraph the highest-leverage location for a direct definitional answer.
sourceCitation: Practitioner consensus 2025-2026 (Frase, Profound, Search Engine Land); aligns with classical featured-snippet optimization literature.

titleTemplate: Add 40-60 word answer capsules after each H2
claim: Self-contained 40-60 word answer blocks placed immediately after each H2 are among the most extractable patterns for AI engines, which often lift them verbatim as citation snippets.
sourceCitation: Practitioner consensus 2025-2026 (Frase, Profound, agency case studies); no controlled study located.
notes: Previously displayed as '+35-40% extraction rate' — that figure has no traceable primary source and has been removed. Strong candidate for internal benchmark: A/B test answer-capsule presence against citation-count on our audited corpus.

titleTemplate: Add a TL;DR or key takeaways section
claim: Summary sections at the top of long-form content are among the most extractable patterns for AI engines, which frequently use them as citation openings and for generating quick answers to user queries.
sourceCitation: Practitioner consensus 2025-2026 (Profound, HubSpot, Search Engine Land); observed in high-citation content across ChatGPT, Claude, and Perplexity.

titleTemplate: Use relevant fan-out questions as headings
claim: Headings that match relevant fan-out questions can make a page easier to retrieve for the related searches AI systems use when building an answer.
sourceCitation: Cyrus Shepard, Zyppy Signal, August 2026: match headings and content to relevant fan-out questions, starting with topics the page already ranks for.

titleTemplate: Cover the most relevant fan-out questions
claim: Expanding an existing page around tightly related fan-out questions can improve coverage of the searches AI systems use to research a topic. Generic FAQ volume is not the goal.
sourceCitation: Cyrus Shepard, Zyppy Signal, August 2026: use People Also Ask and fan-out research, update relevant existing pages first, and avoid creating a separate page for every question.
notes: Previously displayed as '+40% citation likelihood.' That figure has no traceable primary source and has been removed. The recommendation now focuses on relevant query coverage instead of a fixed FAQ count.

titleTemplate: Add structured lists or comparison tables
claim: Structured lists, step-by-steps, and comparison tables are heavily favored by AI extractors over dense paragraph prose.
sourceCitation: Practitioner consensus 2025-2026; aligns with featured-snippet extraction patterns documented across SEO literature.

titleTemplate: Add a comparison table (pricing, features, or alternatives)
claim: Agentic search workflows (OpenAI Operator, Perplexity Comet) browse and compare; pages with machine-readable comparison tables are pulled into agent workflows more often than prose-only pages.
sourceCitation: Practitioner observation 2025-2026 (early agentic-search era); no controlled study yet.

titleTemplate: Break up long paragraphs
claim: Paragraphs over ~120 words are skipped more often by AI extractors than paragraphs of 3-5 sentences.
sourceCitation: Practitioner consensus; aligns with classical readability + featured-snippet guidance.

titleTemplate: Expand topical coverage
claim: Comprehensive sources covering related questions, edge cases, and follow-ups are preferred by AI engines over thin pages.
sourceCitation: Practitioner consensus 2025-2026; aligns with topical-authority SEO literature.

titleTemplate: Add original research, survey data, or proprietary statistics
claim: Content citing original first-party data — brand surveys, internal analyses, customer case studies — is preferentially cited by AI engines because it is a unique source they cannot find elsewhere.
sourceCitation: Practitioner consensus 2025-2026 (Profound, Frase, HubSpot); aligns with GEO paper finding that Statistics Addition is a top-performing method when data is unique and attributed.

titleTemplate: Refresh stale content (last updated ~{age} months ago)
claim: Content older than 24 months earns substantially fewer citations than content updated within the past 12 months. Substantive revisions are detected; cosmetic date bumps are not.
sourceCitation: Practitioner consensus 2025-2026 (Profound, Search Engine Land); no controlled study located.
notes: Previously displayed as '3.2x citation lift moving from >24mo to <12mo' — that figure has no traceable primary source and has been removed. Strong candidate for internal benchmark: we have an audit corpus and can re-audit a sample of URLs after their content is refreshed and measure the citation-count delta.

titleTemplate: Refresh aging content (last updated ~{age} months ago)
claim: Content past the 12-month freshness threshold loses citation share, especially on Perplexity and Google AI Overviews.
sourceCitation: Practitioner consensus 2025-2026 (Profound, Search Engine Land); no controlled study located.
notes: Previously displayed as 'up to 3.2x citation lift returning to <12mo' — that figure has no traceable primary source and has been removed. Same internal-benchmark queue as content-stale-24mo.

titleTemplate: Add a visible "Last Updated" date and current-year markers
claim: Perplexity and Google AI Overviews aggressively deprioritize content with no visible publish date or recent-year reference.
sourceCitation: Practitioner consensus 2025-2026; widely observed but not formally measured.

titleTemplate: Add a machine-readable publish date
claim: Year mentions in body copy are weaker than structured datetime metadata; <time> tags and article:published_time meta let AI engines verify recency unambiguously.
sourceCitation: Practitioner consensus; aligns with schema.org best practices and Google's guidance on dated content.

titleTemplate: Name "{brandName}" in the first 200 words
claim: AI engines match entities by literal name; replacing pronouns and "the platform" with the brand name in opening sections improves entity matching.
sourceCitation: Practitioner consensus 2025-2026; aligns with entity-disambiguation literature.

titleTemplate: State your brand facts plainly
claim: A consistent, factual description of the company helps people and AI systems identify what the business is, who it serves, the problem it solves, and its area of specialization.
sourceCitation: Practitioner consensus 2025-2026; aligns with entity clarity and information-retrieval best practices.

titleTemplate: Add a named-author byline with credentials
claim: Visible author credibility is part of the 2026 baseline for content cited across major AI engines; Claude in particular weights author credentials heavily.
sourceCitation: Practitioner consensus 2025-2026 (HubSpot, Search Engine Land); aligns with Google's E-E-A-T guidance.

titleTemplate: Trim marketing filler
claim: Generic filler phrases ("In today's fast-paced world…", "It's important to note…") dilute information density and contribute no extractable claims.
sourceCitation: Practitioner consensus; aligns with general writing-quality best practices.

titleTemplate: Reduce repeated-keyword density
claim: Traditional keyword-stuffing is actively harmful in generative-engine contexts; AI models penalize obviously over-optimized prose.
sourceCitation: Aggarwal, Murahari, Rajpurohit et al., "GEO: Generative Engine Optimization", KDD 2024 — Keyword Stuffing is identified as a non-performing optimization method (§4, Table 1).
notes: The paper categorizes Keyword Stuffing in a section titled 'Non-Performing Generative Engine Optimization methods' and reports it scores below the unoptimized baseline across both metrics (Table 1: ~17.8 vs 19.5 baseline on Position-Adjusted Word Count). On Perplexity specifically, §4.4 states it 'performs 10% worse than the baseline.' We frame the recommendation as a negative-signal removal rather than a positive-lift intervention.

titleTemplate: Add Article JSON-LD schema
claim: Article markup can describe visible authorship and publication metadata. Keep it accurate and consistent with the page; adding it does not guarantee AI citations.
sourceCitation: Schema.org Article vocabulary. Markup describes content; no citation lift is asserted.

titleTemplate: Add FAQPage JSON-LD schema
claim: FAQPage markup describes visible questions and answers. Use it only where appropriate; do not treat it as a proven AI-citation boost or a guarantee of Google rich results.
sourceCitation: Schema.org FAQPage vocabulary. No universal rich-result or AI-citation eligibility is asserted.

titleTemplate: Add HowTo JSON-LD schema for step-by-step sections
claim: HowTo markup can describe a visible procedure. It does not establish eligibility for special step-level results in Google AI Overviews or guarantee citation.
sourceCitation: Schema.org HowTo vocabulary, not a Google AI Overview rich-result guarantee.

titleTemplate: Add Organization JSON-LD schema
claim: Organization markup can describe your business and verified profiles. Include only accurate identifiers; it does not prove inclusion in any AI system's knowledge graph.
sourceCitation: Schema.org Organization vocabulary. Accurate identity markup does not prove knowledge-graph inclusion.

titleTemplate: Optionally publish an llms.txt file
claim: Server-log studies through 2026 show major AI crawlers almost never request llms.txt, and no major engine has committed to reading it. It is cheap and harmless to publish, but it is not a citation lever. Prioritize crawler access, snippet permissions, and content structure first.
sourceCitation: Crawler-log analyses (Ahrefs, server-log studies) 2026: the overwhelming majority of published llms.txt files receive zero AI-bot requests; Google has stated it does not use the file.

titleTemplate: Unblock AI search and fetch crawlers
claim: If an engine's search indexer or user-request fetcher is blocked in robots.txt, citation in that engine is impossible regardless of content quality. Blocking training-only bots (GPTBot, ClaudeBot, Google-Extended, meta-externalagent) is a separate IP decision that does not affect citations.
sourceCitation: OpenAI and Anthropic crawler documentation: OAI-SearchBot/ChatGPT-User and Claude-SearchBot/Claude-User are controlled independently of the training bots; allowing them governs search citations.

titleTemplate: Restructure passages into self-contained answers
claim: Passages that open with a definition or direct answer and stand alone without surrounding context are extracted more reliably by AI engines than passages requiring upstream context.
sourceCitation: AEO Improvement internal heuristic — passage-citability scoring derived from our own audit corpus. Scoring methodology documented on the methodology page; lift number pending controlled benchmark.
notes: Previously displayed a '134-167 word optimal passage length' figure derived from classical featured-snippet length norms, not from controlled measurement against generative engines. Removed pending an internal benchmark; recommendation framed qualitatively in the meantime.

titleTemplate: Review the page's nosnippet directive
claim: Snippet controls can restrict previews and use on supported search surfaces. Review the intended policy and platform-specific effect before changing them.
sourceCitation: Google Search Central, AI features and your website: supporting links require indexing and snippet eligibility; preview controls limit information on supported Google surfaces.
notes: Does not establish a universal rule across all AI systems. Intentional restrictions must be preserved unless the site owner approves a change.

titleTemplate: Review content hidden by data-nosnippet
claim: The data-nosnippet attribute can keep selected page content out of supported search previews and AI surfaces. Important facts and answers should not be hidden by accident.
sourceCitation: Cyrus Shepard, Zyppy Signal, August 2026: audit noindex, nosnippet, max-snippet, and data-nosnippet controls because they can affect AI visibility.

titleTemplate: Front-load your key answer
claim: AI engines apply per-URL retrieval caps when extracting content. Pages that front-load their primary answer — before preambles, context-setting, or disclaimers — are more likely to have that answer extracted and cited.
sourceCitation: Cyrus Shepard, Zyppy Signal — 'Content Placement' ranks #5 among AI citation ranking factors (score 8.8/10). Google Gemini is specifically noted to use a strict per-URL retrieval cap, making above-fold content placement critical for Gemini citations.
notes: No controlled lift number is published for content placement in isolation. The Zyppy Signal framework assigns a practitioner-consensus score of 8.8/10 based on cross-referencing 54 published AI citation experiments; the ranking reflects expert judgment, not a measured percentage improvement attributable to placement alone.

titleTemplate: Make your core content readable without JavaScript
claim: AI crawlers may not consistently render client-side JavaScript. Core answers, headings, and evidence available in raw HTML are more reliably discoverable and eligible for citation.
sourceCitation: Cyrus Shepard, Zyppy Signal, August 2026: many AI crawlers do not routinely render JavaScript, which can leave important page content invisible even when the browser-rendered page looks complete.

titleTemplate: Review CDN and firewall AI-bot controls
claim: Robots.txt is only one access-control layer. CDN, WAF, and bot-management rules can block legitimate AI search and fetch crawlers even when robots.txt allows them.
sourceCitation: Cyrus Shepard, Zyppy Signal, August 2026: CDN and bot-control platforms can manage AI access independently of robots.txt, so both policies should be checked together.
notes: Detection of an infrastructure provider is advisory, not evidence that it blocks AI bots. The recommendation asks for a policy review rather than claiming a block.
